questions.stem: The profitability index is a variation on which of the following capital budgeting models?
questions.explanation: The profitability index divides the present value of future cash flows by the initial investment, using exactly the same discounted amounts as net present value. NPV states the result as a dollar amount while the index states it as a ratio, which makes it useful for ranking projects of different sizes.
questions.explanationJa: 収益性指数は将来キャッシュフローの現在価値を当初投資額で割ったもので、正味現在価値とまったく同じ割引後の金額を用いる。NPVが結果を金額で表すのに対し、指数は比率で表すため、規模の異なるプロジェクトの順位付けに使いやすい。

questions.stem:
Polo Co. requires higher rate of return for projects with a life span greater than five years. Projects extending beyond five years must earn a higher specified rate of return. Which of the following capital budgeting techniques can readily accommodate this requirement?
Internal rate of | Net present value
return
questions.explanation: Both techniques can handle a higher hurdle for longer projects. Net present value simply discounts those projects at the higher required rate, and internal rate of return computes each project's own return and compares it with the higher hurdle rate. Neither method is restricted to a single company-wide rate.
questions.explanationJa: どちらの手法も、期間の長いプロジェクトに高い要求水準を課すことに対応できる。正味現在価値法は、そのプロジェクトを高い要求収益率で割り引けばよい。内部収益率法は、各プロジェクト固有の収益率を計算し、高いハードルレートと比較すればよい。いずれも全社一律の率に縛られる手法ではない。

questions.stem: A proposed project has an expected economic life of eight years. In the calculation of the net present value of the proposed project, salvage value would be

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excluded from the calculation of the net present value

choices.label: B
choices.text: Included as a cash inflow at the future amount of the estimated salvage value

choices.label: C
choices.text: Included as a cash inflow at the estimated salvage value

choices.label: D
choices.text: Included as a cash inflow at the present value of the estimated salvage value

questions.explanation: Salvage value is a cash inflow received at the END of the project's life, so it must be discounted back to today before being compared with the initial outlay. Including it at its future amount (B) or at face value without discounting (C) would overstate net present value.
questions.explanationJa: 残存価額はプロジェクトの「終了時点」に受け取るキャッシュインフローなので、当初投資額と比較する前に現在価値へ割り引く必要がある。将来価値のまま含めたり（B）、割引せずに額面のまま含めたり（C）すると、正味現在価値を過大に評価してしまう。

questions.stem: A project should be accepted if the present value of cash flows from the project is
questions.explanation: Net present value is the present value of the cash flows less the initial investment, so NPV is positive exactly when that present value exceeds the outlay. Equal amounts (A) give NPV of zero, meaning the project earns precisely the required rate and is a matter of indifference.
questions.explanationJa: 正味現在価値はキャッシュフローの現在価値から当初投資額を引いたものなので、現在価値が投資額を上回るときにNPVがプラスとなる。両者が等しい場合（A）はNPVがゼロ、すなわち要求収益率をちょうど達成する状態であり、採否は無差別となる。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to Quest Co.'s Gold Division:
Sales | $311,000
Variable cost | 250,000
Traceable fixed costs | 50,000
Average invested capital | 40,000
Imputed interest rate | 10%
Quest's return on investment was
questions.explanation: Divisional operating income = $311,000 - $250,000 variable - $50,000 traceable fixed = $11,000. ROI = $11,000 / $40,000 average invested capital = 27.5%. The 10% imputed rate is used for residual income, not ROI.
questions.explanationJa: 部門営業利益 = $311,000 − 変動費 $250,000 − 個別固定費 $50,000 = $11,000。ROI = $11,000 ÷ 平均投下資本 $40,000 = 27.5%。帰属利子率10%は残余利益の計算で使うものであり、ROIには用いない。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to Bala Co. for the year ended December 31, Year 1:
Sales | $600,000
Net income | 100,000
Capital investment | 400,000
Which of the following equations should be used to compute Bala's return on investment?
questions.explanation: ROI decomposes into asset turnover times return on sales: (sales / investment) x (net income / sales) = ($600 / $400) x ($100 / $600), which in the answer's shorthand is (6/4) x (1/6). The sales terms cancel, leaving net income over investment.
questions.explanationJa: ROIは資産回転率と売上高利益率の積に分解できる: (売上 ÷ 投資額) × (純利益 ÷ 売上) = ($600 ÷ $400) × ($100 ÷ $600)、これを選択肢の表記に直すと (6/4) × (1/6) となる。売上の項が約分され、純利益 ÷ 投資額が残る。

questions.stem: The invested capital-employed turnover rate would include
questions.explanation: A turnover rate measures how many dollars of sales each dollar of capital generates, so sales go on top and invested capital underneath. Placing net income in the numerator would give return on investment instead of a turnover measure.
questions.explanationJa: 回転率は、資本1ドルがどれだけの売上を生むかを測る指標なので、分子が売上、分母が投下資本となる。分子に純利益を置くと、回転率ではなく投下資本利益率になってしまう。

questions.stem:
Division A is considering a project that will earn a rate of return which is greater than the imputed interest charge for invested capital, but less than the division's historical return on invested capital. Division B is considering a project that will earn a rate of return which is greater than the division's historical return on invested capital, but less than the imputed interest charge for invested capital. If the objective is to maximize residual income, should these divisions accept or reject their projects?
Project A | Project B
questions.explanation: Residual income rises whenever a project earns more than the imputed interest charge, regardless of the division's historical ROI. Division A's project clears that hurdle and should be accepted even though it would dilute A's average return. Division B's project falls short of the charge and would reduce residual income, so it should be rejected.
questions.explanationJa: 残余利益は、プロジェクトの収益率が帰属利子率を上回れば、その部門の過去のROIがどうであれ増加する。A部門のプロジェクトはこの基準を満たすので、部門の平均収益率を下げるとしても採用すべきである。B部門のプロジェクトは帰属利子率に届かず残余利益を減らすため、却下すべきである。

questions.stem: Residual income of an investment center is the center's

choices.label: A
choices.text: Income plus the imputed interest on its invested capital

choices.label: B
choices.text: Income less the imputed interest on its invested capital

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contribution margin plus the imputed interest on its invested capital

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contribution margin less the imputed interest on its invested capital

questions.explanation: Residual income starts from the center's income and subtracts a charge for the capital it uses: income - (invested capital x imputed rate). Subtracting the charge is what makes the measure show value created beyond the minimum required return. Contribution margin is before fixed costs and is not the starting point.
questions.explanationJa: 残余利益は、事業単位の利益から、使用した資本に対する賦課を差し引いて求める（利益 − 投下資本 × 帰属利子率）。この賦課を控除することで、最低限求められる収益を超えて生み出した価値が表れる。貢献利益は固定費控除前の数値であり、出発点にはならない。

questions.stem: What is the par value of common stock?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The value of the stock that must be entered as equity in the issuer’s financial statements

choices.label: B
choices.text: The value of the stock that must be entered as paid-in-capital in the issuer’s financial statements

choices.label: C
choices.text: A shareholder’s liability celling if the issuer goes bankrupt

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estimated market value of the stock when it was issued

questions.explanation: Par value is a nominal legal amount that fixes the maximum a shareholder can be required to contribute. Once shares are paid up to par, the holder has no further liability to creditors if the issuer fails. It bears no relation to market value, and amounts received above par go to additional paid-in capital.
questions.explanationJa: 額面価額は法律上の名目金額であり、株主が拠出を求められうる上限を定めるものである。額面まで払込みが済んでいれば、発行会社が破綻しても株主が債権者に対してそれ以上の責任を負うことはない。市場価値とは無関係で、額面を超えて受け取った金額は資本剰余金に計上される。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not characteristic of venture capital?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lack of liquidity for some time period

questions.explanation: Venture capital typically begins with a private placement, takes common or convertible equity, and stays illiquid until an exit such as an IPO or sale. There is no fixed minimum holding period; the exit comes when the company is ready, which may be sooner or much later than five years.
questions.explanationJa: ベンチャーキャピタルは通常、私募から始まり、普通株や転換権付の持分を取得し、株式公開や売却といった出口までは流動性を欠いたままとなる。ただし最低保有期間が定まっているわけではない。出口は企業の状態次第であり、5年より早いことも、はるかに遅いこともある。

questions.stem: For the next 2 years, a lease is estimated to have an operating net cash inflow of $7,500 per annum, before adjusting for $5,000 per annum tax basis lease amortization, and a 40% tax rate. The present value of an ordinary annuity of $1 per year at 10% for 2 years is $1.74. What is the lease's after-tax present value using a 10% discount factor?
questions.explanation: Amortization is deductible but is not a cash outflow, so it only affects the tax. Taxable income = $7,500 - $5,000 = $2,500, tax = $2,500 x 40% = $1,000. After-tax cash flow = $7,500 - $1,000 = $6,500. Present value = $6,500 x 1.74 = $11,310. Taxing the full $7,500 would give $9,570 (choice C).
questions.explanationJa: リース償却費は損金にはなるがキャッシュの流出ではないため、税額にのみ影響する。課税所得 = $7,500 − $5,000 = $2,500、税額 = $2,500 × 40% = $1,000。税引後キャッシュフロー = $7,500 − $1,000 = $6,500。現在価値 = $6,500 × 1.74 = $11,310。$7,500 全額に課税すると $9,570（選択肢C）となる。

questions.stem:
Which of the following would a rational investor consider when purchasing an entity for cash?
I. The cash paid to the entity's current shareholders
II. The after-tax cash flow from operations III. The present value of the entity's liabilities
questions.explanation: A cash purchase of the entity means acquiring its obligations along with its operations, so all three matter: the price paid to current shareholders, the after-tax cash the business will generate, and the present value of the liabilities that come with it. Ignoring the liabilities would overstate what the buyer is really getting.
questions.explanationJa: 現金による企業買収は、事業とともにその債務も引き受けることを意味するため、3つすべてが判断材料となる。現株主に支払う対価、事業が生み出す税引後キャッシュ、そして引き継ぐ負債の現在価値である。負債を無視すると、買手が実際に得るものを過大に評価してしまう。

questions.stem: Fluid Company's current assets increased by $120 and current liabilities decreased by $200. Fluid's net working capital
questions.explanation: Net working capital = current assets - current liabilities. Assets rose $120 and liabilities fell $200, so the change is $120 - (-$200) = an increase of $320. Subtracting rather than adding the liability decrease gives the $80 decrease in choice B.
questions.explanationJa: 正味運転資本 = 流動資産 − 流動負債。流動資産が $120 増え、流動負債が $200 減ったので、変化は $120 − (−$200) = $320 の増加となる。負債の減少を加算せずに減算すると、選択肢Bの $80 減少という誤りになる。

questions.stem: Advantage Company writes and receives checks totaling $1,000 daily. It takes five days for Advantage's checks to clear its account, but only three days for Advantage's deposits to be available for use. What is the amount of Advantage's float?
questions.explanation: Disbursement float = $1,000 x 5 days = $5,000, the money still in the account after checks are written. Collection float = $1,000 x 3 days = $3,000, deposits not yet usable. Net float = $5,000 - $3,000 = $2,000 in the company's favour.
questions.explanationJa: 支払フロート = $1,000 × 5日 = $5,000。小切手を振り出した後もまだ口座に残っている資金である。回収フロート = $1,000 × 3日 = $3,000。入金したがまだ使えない資金である。純フロート = $5,000 − $3,000 = $2,000 で、企業にとって有利な方向となる。

questions.stem: When would a business most likely offer credit terms of 2/10, net 30?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The business can borrow funds only at a rate higher than the effective annual interest rate of these terms.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The business can borrow funds at a rate lower than the effective annual interest rate of these terms.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Competitors are offering the same terms and the business has a cash shortage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Competitors are not offering terms and the business has a cash surplus.

questions.explanation: Terms of 2/10, net 30 cost the seller roughly 36% on an annual basis, so they are only worth offering when something else compels it: competitors already offer the same terms, and the seller needs cash sooner. A firm that can borrow more cheaply (B) would borrow instead of granting such an expensive discount.
questions.explanationJa: 2/10, net 30 という条件は、売手にとって年率換算でおよそ36%のコストとなるため、他に事情がある場合にのみ提示する価値がある。すなわち、競合が既に同条件を出しており、かつ自社が早期に現金を必要としている場合である。より低い金利で借りられる企業（B）なら、これほど高コストの割引を与えるより借入を選ぶ。

questions.stem: Raking Company is basing next year's budget on sales of $36 million. Raking offers credit terms of 1/10, n/30 and expects that 80% of sales will be on credit, with discounts taken on 50% of the credit sales. What are estimated discounts taken by customers for next year?
questions.explanation: Work through the layers: credit sales = $36M x 80% = $28.8M; discounts are taken on half of that = $14.4M; the discount is 1% = $144,000. Applying the 1% to all credit sales would give $288,000, and to total sales $360,000.
questions.explanationJa: 段階を追って計算する。信用売上 = $36M × 80% = $28.8M。そのうち半分で割引が利用されるので $14.4M。割引率は1%なので $144,000。信用売上全額に1%を適用すると $288,000、総売上に適用すると $360,000 となり、いずれも誤り。

questions.stem:
Tam Company is negotiating for the purchase of equipment that would cost $100,000, with the expectation that $20,000 per year could be saved in after-tax cash costs if the equipment were acquired.
The equipment's estimated useful life is 10 years, with no residual value, and would be depreciated by the straight-line method. Tam's predetermined minimum desired rate of return is 12%. Present value of an annuity of 1 at 12% for 10 periods is 5.65. Present value of 1 due in 10 periods at 12 % is 0.322.
What is the net present value?
questions.explanation: The savings are a level annual amount, so use the annuity factor: $20,000 x 5.65 = $113,000. Net present value = $113,000 - $100,000 = $13,000. There is no residual value, so the single-sum factor 0.322 is not needed.
questions.explanationJa: 節約額は毎年一定なので年金現価係数を使う: $20,000 × 5.65 = $113,000。正味現在価値 = $113,000 − $100,000 = $13,000。残存価額がないため、一時金の現価係数 0.322 は使わない。

questions.stem:
Tam Company is negotiating for the purchase of equipment that would cost $100,000, with the expectation that $20,000 per year could be saved in after-tax cash costs if the equipment were acquired.
The equipment's estimated useful life is 10 years, with no residual value, and would be depreciated by the straight-line method. Tam's predetermined minimum desired rate of return is 12%. Present value of an annuity of 1 at 12% for 10 periods is 5.65. Present value of 1 due in 10 periods at 12 % is 0.322.
What is the accrual accounting rate of return based on initial investment?
questions.explanation: The accrual rate of return uses accounting income, so depreciation must be subtracted from the cash savings: $100,000 / 10 years = $10,000 depreciation, giving income of $20,000 - $10,000 = $10,000. Based on the INITIAL investment, the rate = $10,000 / $100,000 = 10%. Using the cash savings without deducting depreciation would give 20% (choice B).
questions.explanationJa: 会計的利益率は会計上の利益を用いるため、キャッシュ節約額から減価償却費を控除する: $100,000 ÷ 10年 = $10,000 の減価償却費、利益 = $20,000 − $10,000 = $10,000。「当初」投資額基準なので、利益率 = $10,000 ÷ $100,000 = 10%。減価償却を引かずにキャッシュ節約額のまま計算すると20%（選択肢B）となり誤る。

questions.stem:
Tam Company is negotiating for the purchase of equipment that would cost $100,000, with the expectation that $20,000 per year could be saved in after-tax cash costs if the equipment were acquired.
The equipment's estimated useful life is 10 years, with no residual value, and would be depreciated by the straight-line method. Tam's predetermined minimum desired rate of return is 12%. Present value of an annuity of 1 at 12% for 10 periods is 5.65. Present value of 1 due in 10 periods at 12 % is 0.322.
In estimating the internal rate of return, the factors in the table of present values of an annuity should be taken from columns closest to what amount?
questions.explanation: The internal rate of return is the discount rate that makes net present value zero, so $100,000 = $20,000 x factor, giving factor = $100,000 / $20,000 = 5.00. You then scan the 10-period row of the annuity table for the rate whose factor is closest to 5.00. The 5.65 factor corresponds to the 12% hurdle rate, not to the IRR.
questions.explanationJa: 内部収益率は正味現在価値をゼロにする割引率なので、$100,000 = $20,000 × 係数 から 係数 = $100,000 ÷ $20,000 = 5.00。年金現価表の10期の行で、係数が 5.00 に最も近い率を探すことになる。係数 5.65 は要求収益率12%に対応する値であり、IRRの手がかりではない。

questions.stem: A multiperiod project has a positive net present value. Which of the following statements is correct regarding its required rate of return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Less than the company’s weighted average cost of capital

choices.label: B
choices.text: Less than the project’s internal rate of return

choices.label: C
choices.text: Greater than the company’s weighted average cost of capital

choices.label: D
choices.text: Greater than the project’s internal rate of return

questions.explanation: A positive net present value means the cash flows are worth more than the outlay when discounted at the required rate, which happens only when the project earns more than that rate. Since the internal rate of return IS the project's earned rate, the required rate must be below it.
questions.explanationJa: 正味現在価値がプラスであるとは、要求収益率で割り引いてもキャッシュフローの価値が投資額を上回るということであり、これはプロジェクトが要求収益率を超えて稼いでいる場合にのみ起こる。内部収益率はまさにそのプロジェクトが稼ぐ率なので、要求収益率はそれより低いことになる。

questions.stem:
Helm Foundation is a tax-exempt organization. Helm invested $400,000 in a five-year project at the beginning of year 1. Helm estimates that the annual cash savings from this project will amount to $130,000. The $400,000 of assets will be depreciated over their five-year life on the straight-line basis.
On investments of this type, Helm's desired rate of return is 12%. Information on present value factors is as follows.
At 12% | At 14% | At 16%
Present value of 1 for 5 periods | 0.57 | 0.52 | 0.48
Present value of an annuity of 1 for 5 periods | 3.60 | 3.40 | 3.30
What is the net present value of the project?
questions.explanation: Helm is tax-exempt, so the cash savings need no tax adjustment: $130,000 x 3.60 (the 12% annuity factor) = $468,000. Net present value = $468,000 - $400,000 = $68,000. Depreciation is not a cash flow and does not enter the NPV calculation.
questions.explanationJa: Helmは免税団体なのでキャッシュ節約額に税調整は不要: $130,000 × 3.60（12%の年金現価係数）= $468,000。正味現在価値 = $468,000 − $400,000 = $68,000。減価償却費はキャッシュフローではないため、NPVの計算には入れない。

questions.stem:
Helm Foundation is a tax-exempt organization. Helm invested $400,000 in a five-year project at the beginning of year 1. Helm estimates that the annual cash savings from this project will amount to $130,000. The $400,000 of assets will be depreciated over their five-year life on the straight-line basis.
On investments of this type, Helm's desired rate of return is 12%. Information on present value factors is as follows.
At 12% | At 14% | At 16%
Present value of 1 for 5 periods | 0.57 | 0.52 | 0.48
Present value of an annuity of 1 for 5 periods | 3.60 | 3.40 | 3.30
What is the internal rate of return on this project?
questions.explanation: At the IRR, $400,000 = $130,000 x factor, so the required factor = 3.077. Annuity factors fall as the rate rises, and even the 16% factor is 3.30, still above 3.077. The rate that produces 3.077 must therefore be higher than 16%.
questions.explanationJa: IRRでは $400,000 = $130,000 × 係数 が成り立つので、必要な係数 = 3.077。年金現価係数は割引率が上がるほど小さくなるが、16%の係数でも 3.30 とまだ 3.077 を上回っている。したがって係数 3.077 をもたらす率は16%より高い。

questions.stem:
Helm Foundation is a tax-exempt organization. Helm invested $400,000 in a five-year project at the beginning of year 1. Helm estimates that the annual cash savings from this project will amount to $130,000. The $400,000 of assets will be depreciated over their five-year life on the straight-line basis.
On investments of this type, Helm's desired rate of return is 12%. Information on present value factors is as follows.
At 12% | At 14% | At 16%
Present value of 1 for 5 periods | 0.57 | 0.52 | 0.48
Present value of an annuity of 1 for 5 periods | 3.60 | 3.40 | 3.30
For the project's first year, what would be Helm's accounting rate of return, based on the project's average book value for Year 1?
questions.explanation: Accounting income = cash savings $130,000 - depreciation ($400,000 / 5 = $80,000) = $50,000. Average book value in year 1 = (beginning $400,000 + ending $320,000) / 2 = $360,000. Rate = $50,000 / $360,000 = 13.9%. Using the initial $400,000 instead would give 12.5% (choice A).

questions.stem:
Able Company has two mutually exclusive projects, A and B, which have the same initial investment requirements and lives. Project B has a decrease in estimated cash inflows each year, and project A has an increase in estimated net cash inflows each year. Project A has a greater total net cash inflow.
Diagram I below depicts the original estimate of net cash inflows of each project by year. Diagram II depicts the original estimate of net present value (NPV) of each project assuming various discount rates.
Which of the two projects would have the greater payback period and average accounting rate of return (ARR)?
Payback period | Average ARR
questions.explanation: Project A's inflows start small and rise, so it takes longer to recover the outlay: A has the longer payback period. The average accounting rate of return is driven by total income over the life, and A has the greater total net cash inflow with the same investment, so A also has the higher average ARR. Neither measure discounts, so the timing advantage of B does not help it here.
questions.explanationJa: プロジェクトAはキャッシュ流入が小さく始まって年々増えるため、投資額の回収に時間がかかる。したがって回収期間はAの方が長い。平均会計的利益率は全期間の利益総額で決まり、投資額が同じでAの方が総流入額が大きいので、平均ARRもAの方が高い。どちらの指標も割引を行わないため、Bの「早く回収できる」という利点はここでは効かない。

questions.stem:
Able Company has two mutually exclusive projects, A and B, which have the same initial investment requirements and lives. Project B has a decrease in estimated cash inflows each year, and project A has an increase in estimated net cash inflows each year. Project A has a greater total net cash inflow.
Diagram I below depicts the original estimate of net cash inflows of each project by year. Diagram II depicts the original estimate of net present value (NPV) of each project assuming various discount rates.
Due to innovation, both projects will terminate at the end of Year 4 with cash flows remaining as projected for the first 4 years and no cash flows in Year 5. Which of the two projects would have the greater internal rate of return under the original estimate and the estimate made in light of the new circumstances?
Original estimates | New estimates
questions.explanation: Under the original estimates B earns the higher internal rate of return because its inflows arrive early, and IRR rewards early cash regardless of the total. Cutting off Year 5 removes A's largest inflow while barely touching B, whose cash had already been received, so B remains higher under the new estimates as well.
questions.explanationJa: 当初の見積りではBの内部収益率が高い。Bは流入が早い時期に集中しており、IRRは総額にかかわらず早期のキャッシュを高く評価するためである。5年目を打ち切ると、後年に流入が偏るAは最大の流入を失う一方、Bは既に回収済みでほとんど影響を受けない。したがって新しい見積りでもBの方が高いままとなる。

questions.stem:
Harvey Co. is evaluating a capital investment proposal for a new machine. The investment proposal shows the following information.
Initial cost | $500,000
Life | 10 years
Annual net cash inflows | $200,000
Salvage value | $100,000
If acquired, the machine will be depreciated using the straight-line method. The payback period for this investment is
questions.explanation: Payback divides the initial cost by the annual net cash inflow: $500,000 / $200,000 = 2.5 years. Salvage value is received at the end of the tenth year and therefore cannot shorten the time needed to recover the outlay, and depreciation is not a cash flow.
questions.explanationJa: 回収期間は当初投資額を年間正味キャッシュ流入額で割って求める: $500,000 ÷ $200,000 = 2.5年。残存価額は10年目の末に受け取るものなので投資額の回収期間を短縮できない。また減価償却費はキャッシュフローではない。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a strength of the payback method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It considers cash flows for all years of the project.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It distinguishes the sources of cash inflows.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It considers the time value of money.

questions.explanation: The payback method's appeal is its simplicity: it needs no discount rate and produces a figure that is easy to communicate. Its weaknesses are the mirror image of the other choices, since it ignores cash flows after the payback point, does not distinguish their sources, and applies no discounting.
questions.explanationJa: 回収期間法の利点はその簡便さにある。割引率を必要とせず、結果も伝えやすい。他の選択肢は、いずれも回収期間法の弱点をそのまま裏返した記述である。回収時点より後のキャッシュフローを無視し、その源泉を区別せず、割引計算も行わない。

questions.stem:
Zig Corp. provides the following information:
Pretax operating profit | $300,000,000
Tax rate | 40%
Capital used (50% debt, 50% equity) | $1,200,000,000
Cost of equity | 15%
Cost of debt | 5%
What of the following represents Zig's year-end economic value-added amount?
questions.explanation: NOPAT is pretax operating profit after tax: $300,000,000 x 60% = $180,000,000. The capital charge applies the weighted average cost of the capital employed, 50% x 15% equity + 50% x 5% debt = 10%, to $1,200,000,000, giving $120,000,000. EVA = $180,000,000 - $120,000,000 = $60,000,000. The tax rate is applied to operating profit; the stated 5% debt cost is already an after-tax figure and is not reduced again.
questions.explanationJa: NOPATは税引前営業利益の税引後の金額で、$300,000,000×60%＝$180,000,000。資本費用は使用資本の加重平均コスト、すなわち50%×15%（自己資本）＋50%×5%（負債）＝10%を$1,200,000,000に乗じて$120,000,000。EVA＝$180,000,000−$120,000,000＝$60,000,000。税率は営業利益に対して適用するものであり、与えられた負債コスト5%は既に税引後の数値なので重ねて調整しない。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A call premium is a premium that investors are required to pay when the bond is purchased.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A call provision generally is deemed unfavorable to investors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Convertible bonds must be converted to common stock either prior to, or at, maturity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A sinking fund provision prohibits the issuer from redeeming a bond issue before maturity.

questions.explanation: A call provision lets the issuer redeem the bonds early, and it will do so when rates fall, precisely when the investor would rather keep the high coupon. The investor loses that favorable position and must reinvest at lower rates, so the provision works against investors. A call premium is paid by the issuer, not by investors (A). Convertible holders may let the option lapse and hold to maturity (C). A sinking fund requires periodic retirement rather than prohibiting early redemption (D).
questions.explanationJa: コール条項は発行体が期限前に償還できる権利であり、金利が低下した局面で行使される。投資家にとっては高いクーポンを維持したいときに回収され、より低い利回りで再投資を強いられるため不利に働く。コールプレミアムは発行体が支払うもので投資家が支払うのではない（A）。転換社債の保有者は転換権を行使せず満期まで保有することもできる（C）。減債基金条項は定期的な償還を義務づけるもので、期限前償還を禁じるものではない（D）。

questions.stem:
Balsam Company issued nonparticipating, 8%, cumulative preferred stock. Which of the following
characteristics is not true of this stock?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dividend payments are not tax deductible by Balsam

choices.label: C
choices.text: Higher claim than common stock in the event of liquidation

questions.explanation: Preferred stock ordinarily carries no vote: the trade-off for a priority claim and a fixed dividend is giving up a say in governance, so voting rights is the characteristic that does not hold. Preferred dividends are distributions of after-tax income and are not deductible by the issuer (A), the dividend is fixed at 8% of par (B), and preferred ranks ahead of common in liquidation (C).
questions.explanationJa: 優先株は通常議決権を持たない。優先的な請求権と固定配当を得る代わりに経営への発言権を放棄する設計であり、「議決権」が当てはまらない特徴となる。優先配当は税引後利益の分配であって発行体の損金にはならず（A）、配当は額面の8%で固定され（B）、清算時には普通株に優先する（C）。

questions.stem: What is the primary advantage of zero coupon bonds for an issuer?

choices.label: C
choices.text: No interest expense recognized by issuer until bond maturity

choices.label: D
choices.text: No interest income recognized by purchaser until bond maturity

questions.explanation: A zero coupon bond pays no periodic interest; the entire return comes from the issue discount accreting to face value at maturity. For the issuer the advantage is that no cash leaves the company until the bond matures. Interest expense is still recognized each period as the discount is amortized, so C is wrong, and the purchaser likewise accrues interest income annually (D).
questions.explanationJa: ゼロクーポン債は定期的な利払いがなく、発行時の割引額が満期に向けて額面まで累増することで投資収益が生じる。発行体にとっての利点は満期まで現金が流出しない点にある。利息費用は割引額の償却を通じて各期に認識されるためCは誤りで、購入者側も同様に毎期利息収益を計上する（D）。

questions.stem: What is the primary advantage of serial bonds for a purchaser?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All bonds in an issue mature at the same time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Purchasers may select the maturity that matches their financial goals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bonds are retired by lottery based on serial numbers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The coupon rate is adjusted based on the maturity date.

questions.explanation: A serial bond issue matures in installments on a series of dates rather than all at once, so a purchaser can select the maturity that matches when the funds will be needed. A describes a term bond, C describes redemption by lottery under a sinking fund, and D describes a floating-rate feature.
questions.explanationJa: 連続償還債は発行分が一時に満期を迎えるのではなく、複数の期日に分割して償還される。購入者は資金が必要となる時期に合った満期を選べる点が利点である。Aは一括償還債の説明、Cは減債基金による抽選償還、Dは変動利付債の特徴である。

questions.stem: What is the primary disadvantage of convertible bonds for an issuer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Convertible bonds have higher interest rates than bonds that are not convertible.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Holders of nonconvertible bonds typically accept less restrictive covenants in bond indentures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Investors may choose not to convert the bonds.

questions.explanation: An issuer accepts the lower coupon on a convertible because it expects the debt to turn into equity. If the share price never rises enough, holders keep the bonds rather than converting, and the issuer is left carrying debt it had planned to retire. Convertibles carry lower, not higher, interest rates (A). Conversion adds equity and therefore reduces leverage rather than diluting it (B). Holders of nonconvertible bonds demand more, not less, restrictive covenants (C).
questions.explanationJa: 発行体が転換社債の低いクーポンを受け入れるのは、その負債が資本に転換されることを期待するからである。株価が十分に上昇しなければ保有者は転換せず債券のまま保持し、発行体は解消する予定だった負債を抱え続けることになる。転換社債の利率は非転換債より低い（A）。転換は自己資本を増やすためレバレッジは希薄化ではなく低下する（B）。非転換債の保有者はより緩やかではなくより厳しいコベナンツを求める（C）。

questions.stem: What is characteristic of debentures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Require interest payments only when earnings are sufficient

choices.label: B
choices.text: Secured by the full faith and credit of the issuer

choices.label: C
choices.text: Secured by a lien on specified collateral

choices.label: D
choices.text: A set of covenants that typically restricts the amount of debt that a bond issuer may carry and the dividends it may pay

questions.explanation: A debenture is unsecured: no specific property is pledged, so the holder relies on the general credit standing of the issuer. A describes an income bond, C describes a mortgage or collateral trust bond, and D describes covenants found in indentures generally rather than a defining feature of debentures.
questions.explanationJa: 無担保社債（debenture）は特定の財産を担保に供さず、保有者は発行体の一般的な信用力に依拠する。Aは収益社債、Cは抵当付社債や担保信託社債の説明であり、Dは社債契約全般に置かれるコベナンツの記述で無担保社債に固有の特徴ではない。

questions.stem:
What would be the primary reason for a company to agree to a debt covenant limiting the percentage of
its long-term debt?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To cause the price of the company's stock to rise

choices.label: B
choices.text: To lower the company's bond rating

choices.label: C
choices.text: To reduce the risk for existing bondholders

choices.label: D
choices.text: To reduce the interest rate on the bonds being sold

questions.explanation: Covenants exist to reassure the buyers of the new issue. By contractually capping how much long-term debt it may carry, the issuer lowers the default risk those buyers face, and they accept a lower yield in return. What the company buys with the restriction is a reduced interest rate. Existing bondholders do benefit (C), but that is a side effect rather than the company's reason for agreeing.
questions.explanationJa: コベナンツは新規発行債の購入者を安心させるために置かれる。長期負債の比率を契約で上限設定すれば購入者が負う債務不履行リスクが下がり、その見返りとして低い利回りが受け入れられる。会社が制約と引き換えに得ているのは金利の低下である。既存の社債権者も恩恵を受ける（C）が、それは副次的な結果であって会社が合意する理由ではない。

questions.stem:
The capital structure of a firm includes bonds with a coupon rate of 12% and an effective interest rate is
14%. The corporate tax rate is 30%. What is the firm's net cost of debt?
questions.explanation: The net cost of debt starts from the rate the company actually bears on a market basis, the 14% effective rate, and reduces it by the tax deduction: 14% x (1 - 30%) = 9.8%. The 12% coupon only fixes the cash interest payment and is not the cost of the borrowing.
questions.explanationJa: 税引後の負債コストは、会社が市場ベースで実際に負担する率である実効利率14%を出発点に、損金算入による節税分を控除して求める。14%×(1−30%)＝9.8%。クーポン利率12%は現金の利払額を定めるだけで、資金調達コストそのものではない。

questions.stem:
Reinhold Company is considering a $50 million project in the upcoming year. Reinhold plans to use both
debt and equity to finance the project. Reinhold's beta coefficient is estimated at 0.95. Reinhold has a
30% effective income tax rate. The equity market is expected to have average earnings of 12%. U.S.
Treasury bonds currently yield 4%.
Funds generated from earnings, $35 million.
Additional funds from $15 million 20-year, 6% bonds at a price of 102, with flotation costs of 3% of
par.
The capital asset pricing model (CAPM) computes a security's expected return by adding the risk-free
rate of return to the incremental yield of the expected market return, adjusted by the issuer's beta. What
is Reinhold's expected rate of return using this model?
questions.explanation: CAPM adds to the risk-free rate the market risk premium scaled by beta: 4% + 0.95 x (12% - 4%) = 4% + 7.6% = 11.6%. The financing mix, the tax rate and the bond terms are not inputs to the expected return on equity under this model.
questions.explanationJa: CAPMは、市場リスクプレミアムにベータを乗じたものを無リスク利子率に加える。4%＋0.95×(12%−4%)＝4%＋7.6%＝11.6%。資金調達の構成、税率、債券の条件は、このモデルにおける自己資本の期待収益率の計算要素にはならない。

questions.stem:
Snaps Company will start a $30 million project in the upcoming year. Snaps will use $22.5 million of debt
and $7.5 million of equity to finance the project. Snaps has a 30% effective income tax rate. The after-
tax cost of debt is 6% and the cost of equity is 12%. What is Snaps' approximate weighted average cost
of capital for this project?
questions.explanation: Weight each source by its share of the $30 million: debt is $22.5 million, or 75%, and equity is $7.5 million, or 25%. WACC = 75% x 6% + 25% x 12% = 4.5% + 3.0% = 7.5%. The 6% is stated as an after-tax cost of debt, so the 30% tax rate is not applied a second time.
questions.explanationJa: 各調達源を$30 millionに占める割合で加重する。負債は$22.5 millionで75%、自己資本は$7.5 millionで25%。WACC＝75%×6%＋25%×12%＝4.5%＋3.0%＝7.5%。6%は税引後の負債コストとして与えられているため、税率30%を重ねて適用してはならない。

questions.stem: Which of the following items represents a business risk in capital structure decisions?
questions.explanation: Business risk is the variability in operating results that exists before any financing decision is made; it arises from the entity's operations, and cash flow is its direct measure. Contractual obligations arise from financing and belong to financial risk (A), while management preferences and the timing of information are not risk categories in this framework (B, D).
questions.explanationJa: 事業リスクとは、資金調達の意思決定を行う前から存在する営業成績の変動性であり、企業の事業活動そのものから生じる。その直接の尺度がキャッシュフローである。契約上の債務は資金調達から生じるもので財務リスクに属し（A）、経営者の選好や情報のタイミングはこの枠組みにおけるリスク区分ではない（B・D）。

questions.stem:
Bander Co. is determining how to finance some long-term projects. Bander has decided it prefers the
benefits of no fixed charges, no fixed maturity date and an increase in the credit-worthiness of the
company. Which of the following would best meet Bander's financing requirements?
questions.explanation: Common stock carries no fixed charge and no maturity date, and by enlarging the equity base it improves the debt-to-equity ratio and therefore creditworthiness. Bonds, long-term debt and short-term debt each impose fixed interest and a repayment date, and each adds leverage rather than strengthening credit.
questions.explanationJa: 普通株は固定的な支払義務を伴わず満期もなく、自己資本を厚くすることで負債比率を改善し信用力を高める。社債・長期借入金・短期借入金はいずれも固定的な利息と返済期日を課し、信用力を高めるどころかレバレッジを増やす。

questions.stem: Which of the following involves an imputed cost?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Interest portion of a capital lease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Interest paid on a bank loan

choices.label: D
choices.text: Interest on internally generated cash used to purchase fixed assets

questions.explanation: An imputed cost is never entered in the accounts; it is the return forgone by committing resources to one use instead of another. Using internally generated cash to buy fixed assets sacrifices the return that cash could have earned elsewhere, and no journal entry is made for it. Depreciation and the interest amounts in A, B and C are all recorded.
questions.explanationJa: 帰属原価（imputed cost）は帳簿に記録されない原価であり、資源をある用途に振り向けたことで放棄された収益を指す。内部で生み出した資金を固定資産の購入に充てれば、その資金が他で得られたはずの収益を犠牲にしているが、仕訳は起こされない。減価償却費およびA・B・Cの利息はいずれも実際に記帳される金額である。

questions.stem: The optimal capitalization for an organization usually can be determined by the

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lowest total weighted-average cost of capital (WACC)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intersection of the marginal cost of capital and the marginal efficiency of investment

questions.explanation: The optimal capitalization is the mix that minimizes the weighted average cost of capital, because discounting the same expected cash flows at a lower rate maximizes the value of the entity. Maximizing either leverage measure raises risk without regard to value (A, B), and D describes the optimal level of investment rather than the optimal financing mix.
questions.explanationJa: 最適な資本構成とは加重平均資本コストを最小化する組み合わせである。同じ期待キャッシュフローをより低い率で割り引くことになり、企業価値が最大化されるためである。レバレッジ指標を最大化すること（A・B）は価値を顧みずリスクを高めるだけであり、Dは最適な投資水準の説明であって資金調達構成の話ではない。

questions.stem:
Karma Company finances each asset with financial instruments with maturities with lengths similar to
asset life. What is this policy called?
questions.explanation: Matching the maturity of each financing source to the life of the asset it funds is the hedging, or maturity matching, approach: long-lived assets are financed long term and seasonal needs short term, so the entity is never forced to refinance a long-lived asset in an unfavorable market. Operating and financial leverage describe cost structure rather than maturity policy (A, C).
questions.explanationJa: 各資産の耐用年数に調達源の満期を合わせる方針はヘッジング・アプローチ（満期マッチング）と呼ばれる。長期資産は長期資金で、季節的な需要は短期資金で賄うことにより、不利な市場環境で長期資産の借換えを迫られる事態を避けられる。営業レバレッジや財務レバレッジ（A・C）はコスト構造を表す概念であって満期政策ではない。

questions.stem:
Owens Company sells 500,000 bottles of condiments annually at $3 per bottle. Variable costs are $0.60
per bottle and fixed costs are $110,000 annually. Owens has annual interest expense of $60,000 and a
30% income tax rate.
What is Owens' approximate degree of operating leverage?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin = 500,000 x ($3.00 - $0.60) = $1,200,000. Operating income = $1,200,000 - $110,000 of fixed costs = $1,090,000. Degree of operating leverage = contribution margin / operating income = $1,200,000 / $1,090,000 = 1.10. Interest and tax fall below operating income and do not enter this measure.

questions.stem:
Owens Company sells 500,000 bottles of condiments annually at $3 per bottle. Variable costs are $0.60
per bottle and fixed costs are $110,000 annually. Owens has annual interest expense of $60,000 and a
30% income tax rate.
What is Owens' approximate degree of financial leverage?
questions.explanation: Degree of financial leverage = operating income / (operating income - interest). Operating income is $1,200,000 - $110,000 = $1,090,000 and interest is $60,000, so $1,090,000 / $1,030,000 = 1.06. The tax rate scales income before and after interest by the same proportion and therefore cancels out.
questions.explanationJa: 財務レバレッジ度＝営業利益÷(営業利益−支払利息)。営業利益は$1,200,000−$110,000＝$1,090,000、支払利息は$60,000であるから、$1,090,000÷$1,030,000＝1.06。税率は利息控除前後の利益に同じ比率で効くため相殺される。

questions.stem: Which of the following factors would influence an entity to increase its proportion of debt financing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A decrease in the times-interest-earned ratio

choices.label: C
choices.text: An increase in the effective income tax rate

choices.label: D
choices.text: An increase in the federal funds rate

questions.explanation: Interest is deductible, so the value of the tax shield rises with the tax rate: a higher effective rate makes debt cheaper relative to equity and encourages more borrowing. A falling times-interest-earned ratio signals the entity is already straining to cover interest (A), while economic uncertainty and a higher federal funds rate make debt riskier or dearer (B, D).
questions.explanationJa: 支払利息は損金算入されるため、税率が高いほど節税効果の価値は大きくなる。実効税率の上昇は自己資本に比べて負債を相対的に安くし、借入を促す。インタレスト・カバレッジ・レシオの低下は既に利息の支払いに余裕がないことを示し（A）、経済の不確実性やフェデラルファンド金利の上昇は負債のリスクやコストを高める（B・D）。

questions.stem: Which of the following is an assumption of an active policy strategy for dividends?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The rate of return that investors require is not affected by dividend policy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dividends are irrelevant to investor decisions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dividends provide information to the market.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stock dividends are preferable to cash dividends when management is concerned about control.

questions.explanation: An active dividend policy treats the dividend as a deliberate message: management sets it to convey its own expectations about future earnings, which is the signaling view. A and B are the assumptions of dividend irrelevance, the passive view, and D concerns the form of the distribution rather than whether dividend policy conveys information.
questions.explanationJa: 能動的な配当政策は、配当を意図的なメッセージとして扱う。経営者は将来の利益に対する自らの見通しを伝えるために配当水準を決めるという、シグナリングの考え方である。A・Bは配当無関連命題すなわち受動的な立場の前提であり、Dは配当政策が情報を伝えるかどうかではなく分配の形態に関する記述である。

questions.stem:
Egret Company expects next year's net income to be $2 million. Egret's current capital structure is 30%
debt, 30% preferred equity, and 40% common equity. Next year, Egret's plans to issue debt and common
stock as needed to maintain their 30:40 ratio, not to issue more preferred stock. Interest payments on
Egret's 10,000 4%, $1,000 par value bonds are current. Egret can issue up to $1 million more 4% bonds
at face value. Egret's marginal tax rate is 30%. There are no dividends in arrears on Egret's 10,000
shares of 6%, $1,000 par value cumulative preferred stock. Optimal capital spending for next year is
estimated at $1.4 million. Using a strict residual dividend policy, what is the approximate estimated
common stock dividend payout ratio for the next year?
questions.explanation: Under a strict residual policy the dividend is whatever remains after the equity share of the capital budget is funded from earnings. The 30:40 debt-to-common ratio means common equity supplies 40/70 of the $1.4 million budget, or $800,000. Earnings available to common after the $600,000 preferred dividend (10,000 x 6% x $1,000) are $1,400,000, leaving $600,000 to distribute. Measured against the $2,000,000 of net income, that is a 30% payout ratio.
questions.explanationJa: 厳格な残余配当政策のもとでは、資本予算の自己資本負担分を利益から充当した残りが配当となる。負債と普通株の比率30:40より、普通株が$1.4 millionの予算の40/70すなわち$800,000を負担する。優先配当$600,000（10,000株×6%×$1,000）控除後の普通株主に帰属する利益は$1,400,000であり、分配可能額は$600,000となる。純利益$2,000,000に対して配当性向は30%である。

questions.stem:
Deep Company has 5,000 shares of 7% cumulative, $1,000 par value preferred stock and 50,000 shares
of $100 par value common stock outstanding. Deep last declared and paid dividends on April 30, Year
1, for the year ending March 31, Year 1. There are no dividends in arrears for fiscal years ending March
31, Year 1, or earlier. For the year ending March 31, Year 4, Deep's net income is $1,500,000. Deep
declared a common stock dividend that is 25% of net income for the fiscal year ending March 31, Year
4, to be paid on April 30, Year 4. What is the total amount of dividends to be paid on April 30, Year 4?
questions.explanation: The preferred stock is cumulative and was last paid for the year ended March 31, Year 1, so the dividends for the years ended March 31 of Years 2, 3 and 4 are all owed: 3 x (5,000 x $1,000 x 7%) = 3 x $350,000 = $1,050,000. The common dividend is 25% x $1,500,000 = $375,000. Total dividends = $1,050,000 + $375,000 = $1,425,000.

questions.stem: What is the typical reason for a corporation to use warrants?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To avoid dilution of earnings per share

choices.label: B
choices.text: To improve the current cash flow

choices.label: C
choices.text: To lower the cost of debt

choices.label: D
choices.text: To permit the early buy-back of bonds

questions.explanation: Warrants are attached to a bond issue as a sweetener: the buyer receives the right to purchase shares later and in exchange accepts a lower coupon than the bond would otherwise carry. The issuer's purpose is to lower the cost of the debt. Exercise of the warrants issues new shares and therefore dilutes rather than protects earnings per share (A).
questions.explanationJa: ワラントは社債発行時に付される誘因であり、購入者は将来株式を購入する権利を得る代わりに、本来必要となる利率より低いクーポンを受け入れる。発行体の目的は負債コストの引き下げにある。ワラントが行使されれば新株が発行されるため、1株当たり利益は保護されるどころか希薄化する（A）。

questions.stem: Which of the following are characteristic of the growth or exploitation phase of a product life cycle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High promotional expenses as a percentage of sales.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Profits shrink as direct competition increases.

questions.explanation: The growth phase is defined by sales rising rapidly as the product gains acceptance. Heavy promotional spending relative to sales and the absence of direct competitors belong to the introduction phase (A, B), and profits shrinking as competitors crowd in marks the maturity phase (C).
questions.explanationJa: 成長期は、製品が市場に受け入れられて売上高が急速に伸びることで特徴づけられる。売上に対する販売促進費の比率が高いことや直接の競合が少ないことは導入期の特徴であり（A・B）、競合の参入によって利益が縮小するのは成熟期の現象である（C）。

questions.stem:
Amalgamated Corporation is a public company that is not issuing new stock currently. Bill Charge wants
to invest in Amalgamated. In which market would Bill Charge purchase Amalgamated's stock?
questions.explanation: The company is not issuing new stock, so no primary market transaction is available; shares already outstanding change hands between investors in the secondary market. The debt, real estate and mortgage markets trade instruments other than corporate equity.
questions.explanationJa: 会社は新株を発行していないため発行市場での取引は成立せず、既に流通している株式が投資家間で売買される流通市場（セカンダリー市場）で購入することになる。債券市場・不動産市場・モーゲージ市場は、株式以外の商品を扱う市場である。

questions.stem: Which of the following most likely is said to "make a market" in a particular security?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A dealer in an over-the-counter market

questions.explanation: To make a market is to stand ready to buy and sell a security continuously out of one's own inventory, quoting both a bid and an ask. That is the function of a dealer in the over-the-counter market. Commercial banks, mutual funds and pension funds participate as lenders or investors, not as quoting intermediaries.
questions.explanationJa: 「マーケットメイクする」とは、自己の在庫を用いて特定の証券を継続的に売買する用意があることを示し、買値と売値の双方を提示することをいう。これは店頭市場のディーラーの機能である。商業銀行・投資信託・年金基金は貸し手または投資家として参加するのであって、値付けを行う仲介者ではない。

questions.stem:
A lender and a borrower signed a contract for a $1,000 loan for one year. The lender asked the borrower
to pay 3% interest. Inflation occurred and prices rose by 2% over the next year. The borrower repaid
$1,030. What is the amount worth in real terms, after inflation?
questions.explanation: The $1,030 repaid is a nominal amount, and its purchasing power must be restated at the price level that prevailed when the loan was made: $1,030 / 1.02 = $1,009.80. In real terms the lender earned roughly 1%, the 3% nominal rate less 2% inflation.
questions.explanationJa: 返済額$1,030は名目値であり、貸付時点の物価水準に引き直して購買力を測る必要がある。$1,030÷1.02＝$1,009.80。実質ベースでの貸手の収益は約1%、すなわち名目利率3%からインフレ率2%を差し引いた水準にとどまる。

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is true with regard to financial derivatives?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A forward contract is a forward-based derivative that obligates two parties to trade a series of cash flows at specified future settlement dates.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Due to their extreme risk, extensive purchase of derivatives are more likely to occur when markets are stable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use of derivatives should eliminate risk.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Using derivatives divides financial risk into separate elements that can be exchanged between entities.

questions.explanation: A derivative separates a financial risk, such as a rate, a price or a currency, from the underlying position so that the risk alone can be transferred to a party willing to bear it. A forward obligates a single exchange at one settlement date; a series of cash flows describes a swap. Derivative activity rises when markets are volatile rather than stable (B), and hedging shifts risk rather than eliminating it (C).
questions.explanationJa: デリバティブは、金利・価格・通貨といった金融リスクを原資産のポジションから切り離し、そのリスクだけを引き受ける意思のある相手に移転できるようにする商品である。フォワードは単一の決済日における一度の交換を義務づけるもので、一連のキャッシュフローの交換はスワップの説明である。デリバティブの利用は市場が安定した局面ではなく変動が大きい局面で増え（B）、ヘッジはリスクを移転するのであって消滅させるものではない（C）。

questions.stem:
How do exchange clearinghouses promote liquidity in futures markets?
I. The daily mark to market decreases the risk that the other party to a futures contract will be unable
to meet its obligations on the maturity date.
II. Exchanges develop appropriate incentives so that traders do not assume unwarranted risks.
III. Exchanges use standardized contracts.
questions.explanation: The clearinghouse promotes liquidity by removing counterparty concerns and by making contracts interchangeable. Daily marking to market settles gains and losses as they arise so that no large unpaid exposure accumulates to the maturity date (I), and standardized contracts let any buyer trade with any seller (III). Statement II describes discouraging excessive risk-taking, a prudential aim rather than a source of liquidity.
questions.explanationJa: 清算機関は、取引相手の信用不安を取り除き、契約を互換的にすることで流動性を高める。日々の値洗いによって損益がその都度決済されるため、満期日まで多額の未決済エクスポージャーが積み上がることがなく（I）、契約が標準化されていることでどの買い手もどの売り手とも取引できる（III）。IIは過度なリスクテイクを抑制するという健全性の目的であり、流動性の源泉ではない。

questions.stem:
Larson Corp. issued $20 million of long-term debt in the current year. What is a major advantage to
Larson with the debt issuance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The reduced earnings per share possible through financial leverage

choices.label: B
choices.text: The relatively low after-tax cost due to the interest deduction

choices.label: C
choices.text: The increased financial risk resulting from the use of the debt

choices.label: D
choices.text: The reduction of Larson’s control over the company

questions.explanation: Interest on debt is deductible while dividends on stock are not, so the government absorbs part of the cost of borrowing and the after-tax cost of debt falls below its stated rate. That is the advantage Larson obtains. Financial leverage increases rather than reduces earnings per share when the project earns more than the interest rate (A), and C and D describe disadvantages of debt rather than advantages.
questions.explanationJa: 負債の支払利息は損金算入される一方で株式の配当は損金にならないため、借入コストの一部を税が肩代わりし、税引後の負債コストは表面利率を下回る。これがLarsonの得る利点である。財務レバレッジは、投資利回りが利率を上回る限り1株当たり利益を減少させるのではなく増加させ（A）、C・Dは利点ではなく負債の不利な面の記述である。

questions.stem:
Which of the following terms represents the residual income that remains after the cost of all capital,
including equity capital, has been deducted?
questions.explanation: Economic value-added is operating profit after tax less a charge for all capital employed, including a charge for equity that conventional accounting never records. Free cash flow measures the cash available after reinvestment, market value-added compares market value with capital contributed, and net operating capital is a balance rather than a residual income measure.
questions.explanationJa: 経済的付加価値（EVA）は、税引後営業利益からすべての使用資本に対する費用を控除したものであり、通常の会計では計上されない自己資本コストまで差し引く点に特徴がある。フリーキャッシュフローは再投資後に手元に残る資金を測る指標、市場付加価値は市場価値と投下資本を比較する指標、純営業資本は残余利益ではなく残高の概念である。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding opportunity cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Opportunity cost is recorded in the accounts of an organization that has a full costing system.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The potential benefit is not sacrificed when selecting an alternative.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Idle space that has no alternative use has an opportunity cost of zero.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opportunity cost is representative of actual dollar outlay.

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the benefit given up by choosing one alternative over the next best one. If idle space has no alternative use, nothing is given up by occupying it, so its opportunity cost is zero. Opportunity costs are never entered in the accounts (A), the benefit is by definition sacrificed (B), and no cash actually changes hands (D).
questions.explanationJa: 機会原価とは、ある選択肢を採ることで放棄した次善の選択肢から得られたはずの便益をいう。遊休スペースに他の用途がなければ、それを使っても放棄しているものは何もないため、機会原価はゼロとなる。機会原価が帳簿に記帳されることはなく（A）、定義上その便益は犠牲にされており（B）、実際の現金支出を伴うものでもない（D）。

questions.stem: Which of the following types of bonds is most likely to maintain a constant market value?
questions.explanation: A bond's price moves because its fixed coupon becomes worth more or less as market rates change. A floating-rate bond resets its coupon to the prevailing rate, so coupon and market rate stay aligned and the price stays near par. A zero-coupon bond has the longest duration and is the most rate-sensitive (A), while call and conversion features add their own sources of price movement (C, D).
questions.explanationJa: 債券価格が変動するのは、市場金利の変化によって固定クーポンの相対的な価値が上下するためである。変動利付債はクーポンがその時々の市場金利に改定されるため両者が乖離せず、価格は額面近辺にとどまる。ゼロクーポン債はデュレーションが最も長く金利感応度が高い（A）。コール条項や転換権はそれ自体が価格変動の要因となる（C・D）。

questions.stem:
Quiche Corporation has preferred stock with a market value of $107 per share, a face value of $100
per share, underwriting costs of $5 per share, and annual dividends of $10. Quiche's tax rate is 30%.
What is Quiche's approximate cost of capital for preferred stock?
questions.explanation: The cost of preferred stock is the dividend divided by the proceeds the issuer actually keeps: $10 / ($107 - $5) = $10 / $102 = 9.8%. Par value is not used because the shares sell at market price, and the tax rate is irrelevant because preferred dividends are not deductible.
questions.explanationJa: 優先株のコストは、配当を発行体が実際に手にする手取額で除して求める。$10÷($107−$5)＝$10÷$102＝9.8%。株式は市場価格で売却されるため額面は用いない。また優先配当は損金算入されないので税率は関係しない。

questions.stem: What is the overall cost of capital?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average rate of return that an entity earns on its assets

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cost of an entity's equity capital

choices.label: C
choices.text: Expected rate of return for the risk level that an entity represents

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rate of return on assets that meets the costs connected with employed funds

questions.explanation: The overall cost of capital is the composite rate the entity must earn on the assets funded by all of its capital sources in order to satisfy every provider of those funds. A describes the return actually achieved rather than the rate required, B covers only one component, and C states a required return without tying it to the funds actually employed.
questions.explanationJa: 総資本コストとは、すべての資金提供者の要求を満たすために、それらの資金で調達した資産から企業が稼がなければならない複合的な利率である。Aは要求される水準ではなく実際に達成した収益率の説明、Bは構成要素の一つにすぎず、Cは要求収益率を述べるにとどまり実際に用いられている資金と結びついていない。

questions.stem:
Lemur Company's $10 par value common stock currently sells at $100 per share. Lemur has retained
earnings of $100,000: once this is exhausted, Lemur will raise any more necessary equity capital
through a stock issue. Lemur can raise cash by selling common stock at a $2 per share discount with
a $3 per share floatation cost. Annual cash dividends are $7 per share and are not expected to change.
The estimated after-tax cost of funds raised by long-term bonds is 5%. The estimated cost of funds
raised by preferred stock is 6%. Lemur's preferred capital structure is 30% long-term debt, 20%
preferred stock, and 50% common stock. Not counting the $100,000 of retained earnings, the current
capital structure is Lemur's preferred structure.
What would be Lemur's cost of funds from a common stock sale?
questions.explanation: New shares net the issuer the market price less the discount and the flotation cost: $100 - $2 - $3 = $95. With a constant dividend of $7 and no growth, the cost is $7 / $95 = 7.37%.
questions.explanationJa: 新株発行による手取額は、市場価格から値引きと発行費用を差し引いた$100−$2−$3＝$95となる。配当は$7で一定、成長率はゼロであるから、コストは$7÷$95＝7.37%。

questions.stem:
Lemur Company's $10 par value common stock currently sells at $100 per share. Lemur has retained
earnings of $100,000: once this is exhausted, Lemur will raise any more necessary equity capital
through a stock issue. Lemur can raise cash by selling common stock at a $2 per share discount with
a $3 per share floatation cost. Annual cash dividends are $7 per share and are not expected to change.
The estimated after-tax cost of funds raised by long-term bonds is 5%. The estimated cost of funds
raised by preferred stock is 6%. Lemur's preferred capital structure is 30% long-term debt, 20%
preferred stock, and 50% common stock. Not counting the $100,000 of retained earnings, the current
capital structure is Lemur's preferred structure.
What would be Lemur's cost of funds on retained earnings?
questions.explanation: Retained earnings are equity the company already holds, so there is no discount and no flotation cost to deduct and the full $100 market price is the base: $7 / $100 = 7.00%. It is lower than the cost of new shares precisely because issuing costs are avoided.
questions.explanationJa: 内部留保は会社が既に保有している自己資本であり、値引きも発行費用も控除する必要がないため、基礎となるのは市場価格$100そのものである。$7÷$100＝7.00%。発行費用が生じない分だけ新株より低くなる。

questions.stem:
Lemur Company's $10 par value common stock currently sells at $100 per share. Lemur has retained
earnings of $100,000: once this is exhausted, Lemur will raise any more necessary equity capital
through a stock issue. Lemur can raise cash by selling common stock at a $2 per share discount with
a $3 per share floatation cost. Annual cash dividends are $7 per share and are not expected to change.
The estimated after-tax cost of funds raised by long-term bonds is 5%. The estimated cost of funds
raised by preferred stock is 6%. Lemur's preferred capital structure is 30% long-term debt, 20%
preferred stock, and 50% common stock. Not counting the $100,000 of retained earnings, the current
capital structure is Lemur's preferred structure.
If Lemur raises funds for projects requiring capital of $200,000 and keeps its preferred capital structure,
what would be the approximate weighted-average cost of capital?
questions.explanation: Common equity must supply 50% of the $200,000, or $100,000, and the $100,000 of retained earnings covers it exactly, so no new shares are issued and the cost of common is 7.00%. WACC = 30% x 5% + 20% x 6% + 50% x 7.00% = 1.50% + 1.20% + 3.50% = 6.20%.
questions.explanationJa: 普通株は$200,000の50%すなわち$100,000を負担する必要があり、内部留保$100,000でちょうど賄えるため新株発行は生じず、普通株のコストは7.00%となる。WACC＝30%×5%＋20%×6%＋50%×7.00%＝1.50%＋1.20%＋3.50%＝6.20%。

questions.stem:
Lemur Company's $10 par value common stock currently sells at $100 per share. Lemur has retained
earnings of $100,000: once this is exhausted, Lemur will raise any more necessary equity capital
through a stock issue. Lemur can raise cash by selling common stock at a $2 per share discount with
a $3 per share floatation cost. Annual cash dividends are $7 per share and are not expected to change.
The estimated after-tax cost of funds raised by long-term bonds is 5%. The estimated cost of funds
raised by preferred stock is 6%. Lemur's preferred capital structure is 30% long-term debt, 20%
preferred stock, and 50% common stock. Not counting the $100,000 of retained earnings, the current
capital structure is Lemur's preferred structure.
If Lemur raises funds for projects requiring capital of $1,000,000 and keeps its preferred capital structure,
what would be the weighted-average cost of capital?
questions.explanation: Common equity must supply 50% of $1,000,000, or $500,000. Retained earnings provide the first $100,000 at 7.00% and the remaining $400,000 comes from new shares at 7.37%, so the blended cost of common is ($100,000 x 7.00% + $400,000 x 7.37%) / $500,000 = 7.30%. WACC = 30% x 5% + 20% x 6% + 50% x 7.30% = 1.50% + 1.20% + 3.65% = 6.35%.

questions.stem:
ABC Co. had debt with a market value of $1 million and an after-tax cost of financing of 8%. ABC also
had equity with a market value of $2 million and a cost of equity capital of 9%. ABC's weighted-average
cost of capital would be
questions.explanation: Weights come from market values: debt is $1 million of the $3 million total, or one-third, and equity is two-thirds. WACC = (1/3) x 8% + (2/3) x 9% = 2.67% + 6.00% = 8.67%, approximately 8.7%.
questions.explanationJa: ウェイトは市場価値で決まる。負債は合計$3 millionのうち$1 millionで1/3、自己資本が2/3である。WACC＝(1/3)×8%＋(2/3)×9%＝2.67%＋6.00%＝8.67%、すなわち約8.7%。

questions.stem: Which of the following objectives is consistent with an optimal capital structure?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Minimum weighted average cost of capital

questions.explanation: The optimal capital structure is the financing mix at which the weighted average cost of capital is lowest, because that mix maximizes the value of the entity. Maximizing earnings per share ignores the risk that leverage adds, minimizing the cost of debt alone would push the firm to borrow without limit, and minimizing risk would mean using no debt at all and forgoing the interest tax shield.
questions.explanationJa: 最適資本構成とは加重平均資本コストが最小となる資金調達の組み合わせであり、その構成において企業価値が最大化される。1株当たり利益の最大化はレバレッジが加えるリスクを無視しており、負債コストのみの最小化は際限のない借入を招き、リスクの最小化は負債を一切用いず利息の節税効果を放棄することを意味する。

questions.stem: What is the impact of a purchase of treasury stock with surplus cash from operations?
questions.explanation: Buying treasury stock pays cash out and reduces equity, leaving the same debt against a smaller equity base, so the debt-to-equity ratio rises and financial leverage increases. Assets fall rather than rise (B), equity falls rather than rises (C), and with fewer shares outstanding earnings per share generally increases (A).
questions.explanationJa: 自己株式の取得は現金を支出して自己資本を減少させるため、負債はそのままに自己資本だけが小さくなり、負債比率が上昇して財務レバレッジが高まる。資産は増えるのではなく減少し（B）、自己資本も増えるのではなく減少する（C）。発行済株式数が減るため1株当たり利益は通常は増加する（A）。

questions.stem:
The benefits of debt financing over equity financing are likely to be highest in which of the following
situations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High marginal tax rates and few noninterest tax benefits

choices.label: B
choices.text: Low marginal tax rates and few noninterest tax benefits

choices.label: C
choices.text: High marginal tax rates and many noninterest tax benefits

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low marginal tax rates and many noninterest tax benefits

questions.explanation: The advantage of debt is the interest tax shield, and it is worth most when the marginal tax rate is high. It is worth more still when the entity has few other deductions competing to absorb taxable income, because the interest deduction is then certain to be used. Low rates shrink the shield (B, D), and abundant noninterest tax benefits may leave too little taxable income for the deduction to matter (C).
questions.explanationJa: 負債の利点は支払利息の節税効果にあり、限界税率が高いほどその価値は大きい。さらに、課税所得を吸収する他の控除が少なければ利息控除は確実に使い切れるため、価値は一層高まる。税率が低ければ節税効果は小さくなり（B・D）、利息以外の税務上の優遇が豊富であれば控除を活かすだけの課税所得が残らないおそれがある（C）。

questions.stem: Which of the following is an assumption of the residual theory of dividends?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The rate of return that investors require is not affected by dividend policy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dividend payments should be a percentage of earnings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The number of dividend distributions should be minimized.

questions.explanation: Under the residual theory the firm funds every acceptable investment first and pays out only what is left, which makes sense only if shareholders are indifferent between a dividend now and the capital gain the retained funds produce. That indifference is exactly the assumption that the required rate of return is unaffected by dividend policy. B, C and D describe managed or stable payout policies, which the residual approach rejects.
questions.explanationJa: 残余理論では、採用に値する投資をすべて賄ったうえで残った分だけを配当する。これが成り立つのは、株主が今の配当と内部留保が生む値上がり益との間で無差別である場合に限られる。その無差別性こそが、要求収益率は配当政策の影響を受けないという前提にほかならない。B・C・Dは管理された配当や安定配当の方針であり、残余理論はそれらを採らない。

questions.stem:
In considering the payback period for three projects, Fly Corp. gathered the following data about cash flows.
Cash Flows by Year
Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 | Year 4 | Year 5
Project A | $(10,000) | $3,000 | $3,000 | $3,000 | $3,000
Project B | (25,000) | 15,000 | 15,000 | (10,000) | 15,000
Project C | (10,000) | 5,000 | 5,000
Which of the projects will achieve payback within three years?
questions.explanation: Payback is reached when cumulative inflows recover the initial outflow. Project A invests $10,000 and takes in $3,000 in each of Years 2 and 3, a cumulative $6,000, so it is not recovered. Project B invests $25,000 and takes in $15,000 in each of Years 2 and 3, a cumulative $30,000, recovering during Year 3. Project C invests $10,000 and takes in $5,000 in each of Years 2 and 3, a cumulative $10,000, recovering exactly at the end of Year 3. Only B and C achieve payback within three years.
questions.explanationJa: 回収期間は、累計の流入額が当初の支出額に達した時点で成立する。Project Aは$10,000を投じてYear 2とYear 3にそれぞれ$3,000、累計$6,000にとどまり未回収である。Project Bは$25,000を投じて各年$15,000、累計$30,000となりYear 3の途中で回収する。Project Cは$10,000を投じて各年$5,000、累計$10,000となりYear 3末にちょうど回収する。3年以内に回収できるのはBとCのみである。

questions.stem:
Unity Company has a higher degree of operating leverage than the industry average. Compared to the
industry average,

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unity's profits are more sensitive to changes in sales volume.

questions.explanation: A high degree of operating leverage means fixed costs make up a large share of the cost structure, so each additional sale contributes heavily to profit and each lost sale cuts deeply: profit swings more for a given change in volume. That greater sensitivity is greater risk, not less (B). High operating leverage implies lower variable costs (A), and the financing mix is a matter of financial rather than operating leverage (D).
questions.explanationJa: 営業レバレッジが高いとは、原価構成に占める固定費の割合が大きいことを意味する。売上が1単位増えれば利益への寄与は大きく、減れば利益の落ち込みも大きいため、販売数量の変化に対する利益の振れ幅が大きくなる。この感応度の高さはリスクが低いことではなく高いことを示す（B）。営業レバレッジが高いほど変動費は低く（A）、資金調達の構成は営業レバレッジではなく財務レバレッジの問題である（D）。

questions.stem: Which of the following objectives is consistent with an optimal capital structure?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maximize the total value of the entity

questions.explanation: The purpose of choosing a capital structure is to maximize the total value of the entity, which occurs at the mix that minimizes the weighted average cost of capital. Maximizing earnings per share ignores the risk leverage adds, and minimizing the cost of debt or of equity alone optimizes one component while ignoring its effect on the other and on the overall cost.
questions.explanationJa: 資本構成を選択する目的は企業全体の価値を最大化することにあり、それは加重平均資本コストが最小となる組み合わせで実現される。1株当たり利益の最大化はレバレッジが加えるリスクを無視しており、負債コストまたは自己資本コストの一方だけを最小化する方針は、他方および全体のコストへの影響を顧みずに一構成要素だけを最適化するものである。
